In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How can we train a deep network to perform a sequence of photo retouching operations, using only an unpaired set of images that exhibit the desired style? How can we enable a user to control and customize the retouching result by providing guidance through an interactive interface that allows the user to specify a desired photo style and a set of constraints?

the development of a novel white-box post-processing framework for photo retouching that is trained from unpaired data, and is able to provide users with a better understanding of the editing process.
developing a white-box photo post-processing framework that can be trained on unpaired images to produce retouched images in a way that is interpretable by users.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our approach is able to generate a wide range of retouching effects, and the results are comparable to or even better than those of the state of the art.
our method can produce retouched images that are similar to the ones in the provided photo set, and that users find them to be of higher quality compared to the original images.
our approach can automatically learn to perform retouching operations based on unpaired training data, and it provides the user with an understandable solution rather than a “black-box result.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, we have developed a deep learning system to learn the retouching style from unpaired images.

we present the first white-box photo post-processing framework, which enables a user to control how the system retouches an image by specifying a set of unpaired images that reflect his or her preferences.
we present a novel deep learning approach for automatic photo retouching.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a deep learning system can be trained on unpaired training images and produce results consistent with the retouching style of the provided set.
it is possible to learn to perform retouching from a set of photos that exhibits the desired editing style, without requiring paired training images.
, by using a white-box framework that allows users to control the retouching process, we can achieve better results than black-box systems trained on paired data.
